title: High-resolution ALMA and HST images of q<SUP>1</SUP> Eri: an asymmetric debris disc with an eccentric Jupiter
question: Characterise the asymmetric outer debris belt of q1 Eri at sub-arcsecond resolution using ALMA and HST observations, and consider its relationship to the planetary system architecture, including the known exo-Jupiter q1 Eri b.

data.arrays: Band 6: 41 antennas; Band 7 (2016): 33 antennas; Band 7 (2018): 46 and 43 antennas
data.angular_resolution: Band 6 natural: 0.67 x 0.54''; Band 7 Briggs (robust=1.0): 0.55 x 0.47''; Band 7 uv-tapered (0.5''): ~0.82 x 0.75''
data.sensitivity: Band 7 residual map rms: 15.9 uJy beam^-1; CO J=3-2 spectro-spatially filtered line profile rms: 7.0 mJy (clockwise) and 7.1 mJy (anti-clockwise)

what.value: Stellar age (1.4 +/- 0.9 Gyr), stellar mass (1.1 M_sun), and exo-Jupiter q1 Eri b parameters (a = 2.03 +/- 0.15 au, M sin(i) = 0.93 +/- 0.18 M_J, e = 0.15 +/- 0.08)

evidence.quote: The planet q$^1$ Eri b has a semi-major axis $a{=}2.03{\pm}0.15$ au, with a mass $M \sin(i){=}0.93{\pm}0.18\,M_{\rm{J}}$, and a low-moderate eccentricity of $e{=}0.15{\pm}0.08$ (cite: Marmier13).
based on a stellar mass of 1.1 $M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ (cite: Marmier13).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, average, realign, and image ALMA Band 6 and Band 7 continuum data
recipe.method: Calibrate visibilities with ALMA pipeline, flag outlying points in Band 6, time-average (10s) and channel-average (4 channels/spw) Band 7 data, reweight with statwt, realign phase centres to Gaia DR2 positions using fixvis and fixplanets, concatenate 2016 and 2018 Band 7 datasets with concat, and image using tclean (natural for Band 6; Briggs robust=1.0 and 0.5'' uv-taper for Band 7).
key_parameters: Time averaging = 10 s, channel averaging = 4 channels per spw (Band 7)
Band 6 weighting = natural; Band 7 weighting = Briggs (robust=1.0) and uv-taper = 0.5''
assumptions: Proper motion mu_RA,Dec = (165.83 +/- 0.10, -105.52 +/- 0.10) mas yr^-1 from Gaia DR2

recipe.goal: Process HST scattered light observations and measure scattered light asymmetry
recipe.method: Roll-subtract two HST ACS/HRC F606W coronagraphic orbits separated by 24.9 deg roll angle, iteratively solve for sky and PSF images, median filter cosmic rays, bin to 0.05'' pix^-1, and measure radial offset of the +22 mag arcsec^-2 contour.
key_parameters: Binned pixel scale = 0.05'' pix^-1; contour levels = +22 and +21 mag arcsec^-2

recipe.method: Fit multi-wavelength photometry and ALMA fluxes with a stellar photosphere plus a two-component modified blackbody model (inner warm and outer cool belts) following (cite: Kennedy14; Yelverton19).
key_parameters: Modified blackbody critical wavelength lambda_0 and slope beta_0
assumptions: 2% calibration uncertainty on stellar photospheric parameters and sub-mm stellar flux predictions

recipe.goal: Measure empirical continuum morphology, radial brightness profiles, scale height, and flux asymmetries in image space
recipe.method: Measure PA from 10 deg wedges, extract major and minor axis radial profiles (within ~0.3'' and ~0.5'' strips), derive inclination from peak-to-peak radial averages, convolve deprojected major axis profile with Gaussians to constrain scale height h, integrate fluxes in NE and SW halves within 30-82 au and 30-200 au, and create a mirror-subtracted image.
key_parameters: Gaussian convolution widths sigma_h = 0.6'', 0.8'', 1.0'' for scale height test
assumptions: Inclination i = 77 deg and distance d = 17.34 pc for converting angular to physical projected distances; 10% flux calibration uncertainty on absolute fluxes

recipe.goal: Extract CO J=3-2 spectral line profile and derive upper limit on CO gas mass
recipe.method: Subtract continuum with uvcontsub, image barycentric cube within +/-200 km s^-1 with tclean (0 iterations), apply spectro-spatial Keplerian mask in clockwise and anti-clockwise rotation directions between 38-125 au, compute 3 sigma integrated flux upper limit, and run NLTE excitation code with fluorescence to derive CO gas mass upper bound and CO+CO2 ice fraction.
key_parameters: uvcontsub fit order = 1, exclusion window = +/- 35 km s^-1; tclean iterations = 0; radial integration = 38-125 au; channel spacing Delta v = 0.423 km s^-1; effective bandwidth factor = 2.667
NLTE kinetic temperatures = 10 K, 50 K, 250 K
assumptions: Stellar mass = 1.1 M_sun, radial velocity v_rad = 27.82 +/- 0.15 km s^-1, CO photodissociation time = 120 years

recipe.goal: Fit parametric 3D radiative transfer models (SYM, CL, ECC, CL+ECC) to Band 7 visibilities
recipe.method: Generate 3D dust temperature and 856 um model images with RADMC-3D for four parametric models (SYM, CL, ECC, CL+ECC), sample model visibilities at observed uv-baselines (N_dat = 19,440,912), and fit using MCMC sampler emcee with visibility weight rescaling factor f_sigma ~ 1.6.
key_parameters: SYM: 12 parameters, 120 walkers, 600 steps, 250 burn-in; CL: 18 parameters, 180 walkers, 1600 steps, 1000 burn-in; ECC: 14 parameters, 140 walkers, 1000 steps, 400 burn-in; CL+ECC: 20 parameters, 180 walkers, 2000 steps, 1200 burn-in
assumptions: Grain size distribution a_min = 0.9 um to a_max = 1 cm with power-law slope alpha = 3.5; dust density = 2.7 g cm^-3; composition = 70% astrosilicates, 15% amorphous carbon, 15% water ice

recipe.goal: Derive analytical constraints on maximum planetesimal sizes, total disc mass, stirring bodies, and sculpting planet mass
recipe.method: Use steady-state collisional cascade lifetime (t_coll = 1.4 Gyr) to find lower limit on D_max and M_disc; equate relative velocity v_rel to escape velocity to constrain stirring body size D_max and mass M_body from scale height h; constrain inner-edge sculpting planet mass using RV non-detection upper limit and secular/clearing/migration lower limits.
assumptions: Q_D^* ~ 163 J kg^-1, age = 1.4 Gyr, alpha = -3.5, D_mm ~ 2 cm, M_dust = 0.028 M_earth, M_* ~ 1.1 M_sun, r = 81.6 au, dr ~ 43 au, asteroid density rho = 2.7 g cm^-3

evidence.quote: We find no evidence for CO gas, but set an upper bound on the CO gas mass of $4{\times}10^{-6}$ M$_{\oplus}$ ($3\,\sigma$), consistent with cometary abundances in the Solar System.
From this we can then set an NLTE upper bound CO gas mass of $M_{\rm{CO}} {<} 4 {\times} 10^{-6}\,M_{\oplus}$, the constraint for low collider densities.

evidence.loc: How big are the largest planetesimals, and what does this imply for the disc mass?
evidence.quote: This gives a lower limit largest planetesimal size of $D_{\rm{max}}{\sim}1\,\rm{km}$ and a lower-bound total disc mass estimate of $M_{\rm{disc}}{>}8\,M_{\oplus}$.
If the measured vertical aspect ratio of $h{=}0.04{\pm}0.01$ is due to dynamical interactions in the disc, then this requires perturbers with sizes ${>}1200$ km.

evidence.loc: Are there further constraints from the vertical distribution?
evidence.quote: we find lower bounds on the mass and size of the bodies providing the stirring as $M_{\rm{body}}{>}2.3{\pm}0.5{\times}10^{21}\,\rm{kg}$ and $D_{\rm{max}}{>}1200\,\rm{km}$

answer_key.quantity: Inferred outer sculpting planet mass at ~60 au

evidence.quote: We find the southwest ansa asymmetry is best fitted by an extended clump on the inner edge of the disc, consistent with perturbations from a planet with mass $8\,M_{\oplus} {-} 11\,M_{\rm Jup}$ at ${\sim}60$ au that may have migrated outwards, similar to Neptune in our Solar System.

score_reason: All ALMA, HST, Gaia, and Spitzer/IRS datasets are publicly identified with exact project IDs, epoch coordinates for proper-motion alignment are tabulated, and the visibility modelling equations, dust opacity assumptions, and MCMC setup are well specified; however, custom modelling scripts, MCMC priors, manual flagging commands, and minor tclean parameters (cell size, clean threshold) are not provided.
rediscovery_reason: All three ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the data reduction and parametric visibility modelling workflows use standard public tools (CASA, RADMC-3D, emcee) with clearly tabulated target coordinates and model equations, and the main findings are quantitative morphological parameters, flux ratios, and gas mass upper limits.
